boards.title: Your First Weekend at Pennsylvania State University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence through University Park landmarks, arts, campus resources, and a Friday-night treat.

cards.title: Friday afternoon — Start at Old Main
cards.subtitle: Old Main lobby, University Park
cards.notes: Step inside during weekday visitor hours to view the land-grant frescoes, then use the lobby as a visual anchor before continuing across campus.
cards.short_summary: A historic first stop centered on the murals inside Penn State’s landmark administration building.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State says visitors can view Old Main’s land-grant frescoes weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.; the mural installation covers more than 1,300 square feet.
cards.source_title: Hidden Gems: The land-grant frescoes at Old Main
cards.access_notes: Penn State states that visitors can stop in weekdays, 8 a.m.–5 p.m., to view the frescoes.

cards.title: Friday afternoon — Find the Nittany Lion Shrine
cards.subtitle: University Park campus landmark
cards.notes: Walk over for an exterior photo and take a moment to orient yourself; keep this stop simple and avoid climbing on the sculpture or surrounding rocks.
cards.short_summary: A named campus sculpture and recognizable outdoor meeting point.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State identifies the Nittany Lion Shrine at University Park as a landmark that draws visitors and is recognized as one of Pennsylvania’s most photographed landmarks.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; follow posted campus rules and respect the sculpture.

cards.title: Friday late afternoon — Browse opportunities at the HUB
cards.subtitle: HUB-Robeson Center, University Park
cards.notes: Stop by the Engagement Space to identify one organization, project, or opportunity worth following up on after your first weekend.
cards.short_summary: A campus-based place to turn early curiosity into a concrete next step.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Engagement Network says its Engagement Space is in the HUB-Robeson Center and is equipped with tools and staff to help students identify goals and available opportunities.
cards.access_notes: The space is in the HUB-Robeson Center; ask staff about current availability and programs.

cards.title: Friday early evening — See the HUB galleries
cards.subtitle: First floor of the HUB-Robeson Center
cards.notes: Take a short gallery loop through the HUB Gallery, Art Alley, and exhibition cases; personal photography is encouraged unless an exhibit says otherwise.
cards.short_summary: A free art stop built into the student union’s public spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State says HUB-Robeson Galleries exhibitions are free and open to all, with locations including the HUB Gallery, Art Alley, and exhibition cases on the first floor.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; personal photography is encouraged unless otherwise noted.

cards.title: Friday night — Visit the Berkey Creamery
cards.subtitle: Corner of Bigler and Curtin Roads
cards.notes: Choose from the current in-store selection and confirm flavors if one matters to you; use the posted location rather than relying on an old campus pin.
cards.short_summary: A campus dairy store with a documented University Park location and evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Berkey Creamery states that its store is at Bigler and Curtin Roads on the University Park campus and lists Friday and Saturday hours until 10 p.m.
cards.source_title: The Store | Penn State Berkey Creamery
cards.access_notes: Posted regular hours: Friday and Saturday 9 a.m.–10 p.m.; check the Creamery page for holiday closures or changes.

cards.title: Saturday morning — Walk the Arboretum
cards.subtitle: East Park Avenue and Bigler Road, University Park
cards.notes: Follow the accessible major walkways through the botanic gardens and bring water; stay on paths and plan to finish before dusk.
cards.short_summary: A free, self-guided outdoor walk through Penn State’s living plant collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arboretum states that it is open daily from dawn to dusk and that there is no admission charge for the H.O. Smith Botanic Gardens or Arboretum land beyond the gardens.
cards.source_title: Hours, Admission, Directions, Parking - The Arboretum at Penn State
cards.access_notes: Open daily dawn to dusk; Penn State notes that all major walkways are accessible.

cards.title: Saturday midday — Enter the Palmer Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: University Park campus museum
cards.notes: Reserve a free timed-entry ticket if available, then move through the galleries at your own pace and check museum guidance before taking photos.
cards.short_summary: A free campus museum visit with timed entry encouraged by the museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Palmer Museum of Art states that admission is always free and encourages visitors to reserve a free timed-entry ticket to guarantee entrance.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; the museum encourages a free timed-entry reservation. Confirm current gallery hours and ticketing before leaving.

cards.title: Saturday afternoon — Settle into Pattee/Paterno
cards.subtitle: Pattee/Paterno Library, University Park
cards.notes: Use the library’s public computer labs or printers to handle one practical task, such as checking course systems or organizing your upcoming week.
cards.short_summary: A practical campus-resource stop with publicly listed computer-lab hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State IT lists two computer labs, hallway stations, and printers at Pattee/Paterno Library and publishes University Park operating hours for the location.
cards.access_notes: Penn State IT lists hours for the Pattee/Paterno location; verify the current schedule before visiting, especially between terms.

cards.entity_name: Sensory-Friendly Libraries Rooms W023 and W027
cards.title: Saturday afternoon — Locate a quiet reset space
cards.subtitle: Collaboration Commons, West Pattee Library
cards.notes: If a quieter pause would help, locate the two sensory rooms in West Pattee; they are not reservable, so use them considerately and share the space.
cards.short_summary: Two named, walk-in sensory rooms intended for quiet comfort and focused activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State’s Sensory-Friendly Libraries site says rooms W023 and W027 are on the ground floor of West Pattee Library, are not reservable, and are open to anyone who wants to use them.
cards.access_notes: Rooms W023 and W027 are not reservable and are open to anyone; treat them as shared quiet spaces.

cards.title: Sunday morning — Walk by Beaver Stadium
cards.subtitle: East side of the University Park campus
cards.notes: Use the stadium exterior as the final landmark on your loop, and check campus notices before approaching because revitalization work is ongoing.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus stadium whose exterior can anchor an east-campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State documents that Beaver Stadium was moved and reassembled on the east side of the University Park campus in 1960; current university reporting says revitalization construction began after the 2024 season.
cards.source_title: Intercollegiate Athletics unveils details on Beaver Stadium Revitalization
cards.access_notes: View from public exterior areas only. Penn State reports active revitalization work; obey barriers, event controls, and posted access limits.
